reason: `open` is an epoch-millisecond instant destructured from nySession() on the line before, divided to the bars' seconds; the line alone reads as a price named open.
`close` is the session's closing instant from the same nySession() call, milliseconds to seconds; not the closing price.

The house simulator's reference wall: 20,000 contracts of open interest x gamma x the contract's 100 shares x price^2 — the exposure arithmetic of a seeded shelf, the literal OI unnamed on the line; no vendor unit is changed.
`r.m` is a store row's minute as an epoch millisecond, divided to the seconds wallObsOf takes as `time`; the strike and value beside it are untouched.

line-pattern: const vega = blackScholesGreeks\(spot, q\.strike, t, iv, r, 0\)\.vega \* 100;
